newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $62, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $62, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle early Thursday were lightly bid at $62.00 per cwt and passed by owners pricing cattle at $63.00, feedlot sources said.
This week's sales were said to be nearly completed following trade Tuesday and Wednesday at $63.00, down $1.00 from last week.
Showlists in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area were close to sold out, with a weekly movement estimated near 100,500 head through Wednesday.
Kansas showlists still had cattle left to sell, with 78,000 head movement estimated so far this week.
Fed cattle prices this week were lower amid outlooks for lighter packer demand during next week's holiday-shortened operations because of the Independence Day holiday on Friday, they said.

Perceptions that beef prices had topped lent further pressure as did feedlot ambitions to remain as current as possible amid knowledge that upcoming cattle numbers were increasing and finishing quickly to market weights, sources said.
Beef prices on Wednesday were quoted down $0.33 to $1.32 per cwt, with 464 fabricated beef loads sold, USDA reported. Heavyweight choice beef fell $102.29, down $1.32 from Tuesday.
Beef prices were pressured by recent large cattle slaughter, which spurred 'fire sale' prices as packers discounted heavily to move the beef, sources said.
